subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw uninstall doesnt remove from .bashrc and commands

question: Should `openclaw uninstall` remain limited to OpenClaw-owned state and marked shell-completion entries, or should it also attempt to remove the global package and installer-managed PATH setup?
rationale: The linked implementation has a clear safe boundary for marked completion entries, while the remaining requested cleanup crosses package-manager ownership and an unmarked shell-config line.

options.title: Keep package removal separate
options.body: Land the marked completion cleanup and document that globally installed CLI binaries must be removed through the package manager.

options.title: Define a broader uninstall contract
options.body: Specify a safe, marker-bounded installer block and package-manager behavior before extending uninstall beyond completion cleanup.

recommendation.title: Keep package removal separate
recommendation.body: Land the marked completion cleanup and document that globally installed CLI binaries must be removed through the package manager.

likelyOwner.reason: Their linked implementation documents the current safe boundary and the tradeoff around broader cleanup.
